text: EX-99.1 2 aap-ex99_1.htm EX-99.1 EX-99.1 Exhibit 99.1 Advance Auto Parts Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results; Updates Full Year 2026 Guidance l Comparable Sales Trends Improved Sequentially During Q3 2026; Turned Positive In the Final Four Weeks l FY 2026 Free Cash Flow Guidance Raised To Approx. $150 Million; Over $400 Million Growth Year-over-Year RALEIGH, N.C., November 5, 2026 — Advance Auto Parts, Inc. (NYSE: AAP), a leading automotive aftermarket parts provider in North America, that serves both professional installer and do-it-yourself customers, announced its financial results for the third quarter ended October 10, 2026. "Our comparable sales performance improved as the quarter progressed. Main Street Pro outperformed throughout the quarter while DIY trends improved compared to the softer trends experienced during the summer. I thank the team for their hard work and commitment to serving our customers," said Shane O'Kelly, president and chief executive officer. "Sales declined in the low-single-digit range during the first eight weeks before turning positive in the final four weeks, supported by improved transaction volumes. The Pro channel led performance in Q3, with low-single-digit sales growth including stronger Main Street Pro growth. The DIY channel declined in the low-single-digit range for the quarter, with trends recovering from negative mid-single-digit levels at the start of the quarter. Despite the volatile demand environment and industry cost pressures, we delivered an adjusted operating margin of 4.5% in Q3 and generated over $100 million of free cash flow year-to-date. We believe that our strategic initiatives are starting to gain traction and we remain focused on delivering sustainable, profitable growth over the long term." Third Quarter 2026 Results ( 1 ) Third quarter 2026 net sales totaled $2,012 million, compared with $2,036 million in the third quarter of the prior year. Comparable store sales for the third quarter 2026 decreased 1.2%. The Company's third quarter 2026 gross profit was $897 million, or 44.6% of net sales compared with $881 million, or 43.3% in the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted gross profit was $899 million, or 44.7% of net sales in the third quarter of 2026 compared with $913 million, or 44.8% in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease in gross profit as a percentage of net sales compared to the third quarter of 2025 was primarily driven by changes in product and channel sales mix compared to last year and supply chain expense deleverage. The Company's third quarter 2026 selling, general and administrative (SG&A) expenses were $850 million, or 42.2% of net sales compared with $859 million, or 42.2% of net sales in the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted SG&A expenses were $808 million, or 40.2% of net sales in the third quarter of 2026 compared with $823 million, or 40.4% of net sales in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease in SG&A as a percentage of net sales compared to the third quarter of 2025 was primarily driven by a reduction in expenses compared to last year, supported by disciplined expense management. The Company's third quarter 2026 operating income was $47 million, or 2.3% of net sales, compared with $22 million, or 1.1% of net sales in the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted operating income was $91 million or 4.5% of net sales in the third quarter of 2026, compared with $90 million or 4.4% of net sales in the third quarter of 2025. The Company's third quarter 2026 diluted earnings per share was $0.25, compared with loss of $0.02 in the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted diluted earnings per share was $0.79 in the third quarter of 2026, compared with $0.92 in the third quarter of 2025. About Advance Auto Parts Advance Auto Parts, Inc. is a leading automotive aftermarket parts provider that serves both professional installers and do-it-yourself customers. As of October 10, 2026, Advance operated 4,325 stores primarily within the United States, with additional locations in Canada, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. The Company also served 787 independently owned Carquest branded stores across these locations in addition to various Caribbean islands. Additional information about Advance, including employment opportunities, customer services, and online shopping for parts, accessories and other offerings can be found at www.AdvanceAutoParts.com. Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures The Company uses certain Non-GAAP financial measures described below to supplement the Company's unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements prepared and presented in accordance with GAAP and to understand and evaluate the Company's core operating performance. These Non-GAAP financial measures, which may be different than similarly titled measures used by other companies, are presented as the Company believes that such Non-GAAP financial measures provide useful information about our financial performance, enhance the overall understanding of our past performance and future prospects, and allow for greater transparency with respect to important metrics used by management for financial and operational decision-making. The Company is presenting these Non-GAAP metrics to provide investors insight to the information used by our management to evaluate our business and financial performance. The Company believes that these measures provide investors increased comparability of our core financial performance over multiple periods with other companies in our industry. The Company's Non-GAAP financial measures include Adjusted Gross Profit, Adjusted Gross Profit Margin, Adjusted Selling, General and Administrative expense (“Adjusted SG&A”), Adjusted SG&A Margin, Adjusted Operating Income (loss), Adjusted Operating Income (loss) Margin, Adjusted Net Income (loss), Adjusted Diluted Earnings (loss) Per Share (“Adjusted Diluted EPS”), Free Cash Flow and Adjusted Net Debt to Adjusted EBITDAR ("Net Leverage Ratio"), and should not be used as a substitute for GAAP financial measures, or considered in isolation, for the purpose of analyzing operating performance, financial position or cash flows. The Company has presented these Non-GAAP financial measures as the Company believes that the presentation of the financial results that exclude the categories of expenses and income listed below provide useful and indicative information about the performance of the Company's base operations because the expenses and income vary from period to period in terms of size, nature and significance. The Company also adjusts for the income tax impact of these Non-GAAP adjustments using the estimated tax rate in effect for the respective Non-GAAP adjustments. Included below is a description of the categories of expenses and income that the Company has determined are not normal, recurring cash operating expenses necessary to operate the Company’s business. • Restructuring and other related expenses: Expenses directly incurred relating to announced restructuring initiatives. These expenses include severance expense, retention bonuses, incremental reserves related to the collectibility of receivables (inclusive of notes receivable) and third-party professional services expenses incurred for services provided in assisting in the development and execution of the plan(s). These expenses also include certain costs related to the distribution network optimization plan for the conversion of the stores and distribution centers to market hubs, including realized losses on liquidated inventory, temporary labor, nonrecurring professional service fees and team member severance. • Impairments and write-down of assets: Expenses relating to the impairment of certain assets, including operating lease right-of-use ("ROU") assets, property and equipment, goodwill and intangible assets. These expenses also include incremental depreciation as a result of accelerating long-lived assets over a shorter useful life, ROU asset amortization after store closure, and incremental lease abandonment expenses as a result of accelerating ROU asset amortization for leases the Company expects to exit before the end of the contractual term, net of gains on lease terminations. • Other items: Expenses primarily relating to nonrecurring services rendered by third-party vendors engaged to perform strategic business review and transformational activities, expense incurred related to acquisitions and divestitures including third-party transaction related expenses, transition services agreement expenses and income, and certain other expenses not viewed as normal cash operating expenses. In fiscal 2025, these expenses also included a non-cash charge related to expected future credit losses on vendor receivables due from a vendor that filed voluntary petitions for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection. Other items also include certain tax items, both expenses and benefits, that are unrelated to the fiscal year in which they are recorded and are excluded in order to provide a clearer understanding of the Company’s ongoing Non-GAAP tax rate and after-tax earnings.
